The technique was introduced in the context of interactive volume rendering using multi-dimensional transfer functions, where high sampling rates were necessary to smooth boundaries between materials but caused unacceptable latency during user interaction [S2, S3][S4, unofficial].

The evidence in sources S2, S3, and S4 explicitly states that high sampling rates (6 to 10 samples per voxel) are necessary to render boundaries smoothly. It further confirms that these high rates cause unacceptable latency (nearly two seconds on Octane2, nearly one second on GeForce3) during user interaction, which necessitates lowering the sampling rate during interaction to maintain interactivity.
